sn5.2:1.2: For Pasenadi’s wife of the same name, see [mn90:3.1]() and note.
sn5.2:2.3: | “Two-inch wisdom” is variously explained by commentaries as limited wisdom; or because women hold thread between two fingers; or because they test whether rice is cooked by pressing a grain between two fingers.
sn5.2:5.1: Somā’s verses at [thig3.8]() lack this verse.
sn5.2:5.3: Reading asmīti with other translators. But surely the Upanishadic echoes should be preserved here; it gets lost if we abbreviate “I’m”. She’s not just dismissing other conceptions of ultimate gender identity, but even the supposed post-gender Upanishadic self.
